pr_body:
This PR:

* Implements the `JsonSourceGenerationOptionsAttribuet.UseStringEnumConverter` property.
* Implements the `JsonNumberEnumConverter<TEnum>` converter.

Fix #87195.

Issue Details
> * While we can register the convert globally, there is no good way to ensure all enums are registered _Originally posted by @terrajobst in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/79311#issuecomment-1579280774_
Author: eiriktsarpalis
Assignees: -

Milestone: -

review_comments: Does an equivalent option not make sense on JsonSerializerOptions?  My understanding is we're now trying to keep them in sync for any options that aren't specifically focused on one mode or the other.

While we could add such a flag to `JsonSerializerOptions`, it would only work in runtimes that support dynamic code (each `Enum` type would require instantiating a `JsonStringEnumConverter<Enum>` at runtime). Effectively such a mechanism already exists, as users can just register the untyped `JsonStringEnumConverter` with their `JsonSerializerOptions` instances, so this flag is a compile-time only AOT-safe substitute.
How did this class not end up in System.Text.Json.Serialization.Converters?
I think that namespace is only used for internal converters, I don't think it's necessary for public stuff.
